responsibility: `rustc_mir_transform` is the compiler crate that owns MIR-to-MIR processing after MIR construction: it defines the pass framework and query entry points in `lib.rs` and `pass_manager.rs`, builds shim MIR in `shim.rs`, and assembles the staged pipelines that validate, normalize, lint, instrument, lower, optimize, and clean up MIR so it is suitable for const checking, borrowck aftermath, code generation, and metadata queries. Its transformation and lowering passes make MIR explicit and runtime-ready: `generator.rs` lowers generators/async bodies into state machines; `inline.rs` together with `rustc_mir_transform::inline` performs callsite inlining while preventing recursive or cyclic expansion; `elaborate_drops.rs`, `remove_uninit_drops.rs`, `remove_unneeded_drops.rs`, and `add_moves_for_packed_drops.rs` make drop behavior explicit, safe, and minimal; `abort_unwinding_calls.rs`, `ffi_unwind_calls.rs`, and `remove_noop_landing_pads.rs` enforce unwind and panic-strategy requirements; `lower_intrinsics.rs`, `lower_slice_len.rs`, `elaborate_box_derefs.rs`, `reveal_all.rs`, `deaggregator.rs`, `deref_separator.rs`, `add_retag.rs`, `add_call_guards.rs`, and `required_consts.rs` rewrite higher-level MIR constructs into simpler, more explicit forms needed by later analyses and codegen; and `coverage` injects MIR-based source-coverage instrumentation and prepares coverage metadata. The crate also contains MIR-based diagnostics and linting passes that enforce language rules or report likely mistakes, including `check_unsafety.rs` for unsafety checking and related lints, `check_const_item_mutation.rs`, `check_packed_ref.rs`, `const_prop_lint.rs` for provable assertion failures, and `function_item_references.rs`, while `dump_mir.rs` provides debugging/test dumps of pass results. For optimization, it supplies both analysis machinery and many canonical MIR optimizations: `const_prop.rs` provides interpreter-backed constant-propagation support, while `dataflow_const_prop.rs`, `const_goto.rs`, `normalize_array_len.rs`, `separate_const_switch.rs`, `simplify_branches.rs`, `simplify_comparison_integral.rs`, `uninhabited_enum_branching.rs`, `unreachable_prop.rs`, `early_otherwise_branch.rs`, `match_branches.rs`, and `simplify_try.rs` fold known control flow and values; `instcombine.rs` performs local peephole simplifications; `dest_prop.rs`, `nrvo.rs`, `sroa.rs`, `dead_store_elimination.rs`, `deduplicate_blocks.rs`, `multiple_return_terminators.rs`, and `remove_zsts.rs` reduce unnecessary temporaries, stores, blocks, and zero-sized work; `simplify.rs` and `remove_false_edges.rs` provide the core CFG and local cleanup infrastructure used across the pipeline; `cleanup_post_borrowck.rs`, `remove_storage_markers.rs`, and `const_debuginfo.rs` strip analysis-only artifacts while preserving useful debug information. Finally, the crate computes MIR-derived metadata consumed by later compiler stages: `deduce_param_attrs.rs` infers optimization-relevant parameter attributes from optimized MIR. Together, these modules make `rustc_mir_transform` the central crate for turning built MIR into explicit, validated, optimized, and instrumented MIR that the rest of rustc can safely analyze and lower.
